label: UniFi Dream Machine Pro Max
description: Ubiquiti UDM-Pro-Max - 1U cloud gateway with two NVR bays: 8x 1GbE RJ45 + 1x 2.5GbE RJ45 (up to 8 WAN ports, no PoE on any port), 2x 10G SFP+; 5 Gbps IDS/IPS.
notes:
Vendor figures read 2026-11-19 from two Ubiquiti hosts, both server-rendered, both quoting the same census. `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro-max` (HTTP 200, 677,375 B) prints the structured spec table: **Port Layout - 1 GbE RJ45 = 8 (1G/100M/10M), 2.5 GbE RJ45 = 1 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M), 10G SFP+ = 2 (10G/1G)**, **Max. WAN Port Count = 8**, **Default WAN Ports = (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45**, **Max. Power Consumption = 60W**, **Power Method = (1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 2A Max., 50/60 Hz / (1) USP-RPS DC input, 11.5V DC, 8.7A**, **NVR Storage = (2) 3.5\" NVR HDD bays** with a built-in 128 GB SSD, **IDS/IPS Throughput = 5 Gbps**. The eleven interfaces above are those rows and nothing else: nine copper sockets (eight 1G behind the 2.5G one) and two 10G cages. The Console and MGMT rows other UniFi gateway pages carry are absent here, so none is modelled.

`https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-pro-max` (HTTP 200, 598,527 B, `displaySku` `UDM-Pro-Max`) carries the same table as embedded spec JSON and settles the PoE question the tech-spec page only settles by silence: **PoE Support = Empty**, **PoE Budget = Empty**, **Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE - PoE / PoE+ / PoE++ / PoE+++ = Empty**, **Voltage Range PoE Mode = Empty**, against **Port Layout = (8) 1 GbE, (1) 2.5 GbE & (2) 10G SFP+**. The model therefore has no PSE port and no budget - which is the one place it differs from its sibling `udm-se.json` (8 PoE ports, 180 W). Copying the SE numbers onto this row is the family-sibling error this catalogue has already corrected on UDM PoE, two i-MO console ports and three MA5801 uplinks; the "Empty" flags are the vendor saying the field does not apply, not the vendor omitting it.

The nine copper ports carry `poeIn: false` on purpose. The engine infers a 12.95 W 802.3af **draw** on copper ports of any device whose model or label matches `unifi` (`isPoePd` in `engine/media.js`), which is right for an access point and wrong for a rack console: this box is powered by a 100 W internal AC supply or the USP-RPS DC input, and neither the tech-spec table nor the store table publishes a PoE *input*. Declaring the port stops the engine turning that silence into a phantom load a lab could spend against a switch budget. `dl.ui.com/ds/udm-pro-max_ds.pdf` was tried and falls back to the 609,911-byte techspecs home page, so no datasheet is cited here.

LAN bank is one bridge (measured 2026-11-20 23:5x UTC). `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro-max` (HTTP 200, 677,375 B, server-rendered spec table) prints **LACP Port Aggregation** and **MAC Address Table Size = 4,000** in its Networking section, next to `Port Layout - 1 GbE RJ45 = 8 (1G/100M/10M)`; the storefront payload for the same SKU (`https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-pro-max`, HTTP 200, 598,660 B) repeats both rows and attaches the note "GbE RJ45 ports 1-8" to the LACP entry. A LAG over the eight 1G sockets is a switch feature - routed interfaces cannot be bundled - and a 4,000-entry MAC table is a bridge FDB, so Port 1-Port 8 forward at layer 2 and the row now declares `l2-forward` (MAC learning + flooding; VLAN, LAG and STP run on any such box). Without the token the console refused `switchport access vlan` and `channel-group`, and two hosts on Port 1 and Port 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP - their frames were dropped as "not addressed to this device". `no switchport` still routes a port; the WAN port and both SFP+ cages keep their addresses.

WAN/LAN separation, read 2026-11-21. Ubiquiti's controller device database numbers the sockets and names the uplink: https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UDM-Pro-Max) prints `ports` = {"eth0": "LAN", "eth1": "LAN", "eth2": "LAN", "eth3": "LAN", "eth4": "LAN", "eth5": "LAN", "eth6": "LAN", "eth7": "LAN", "eth8": "WAN", "eth9": "WAN2", "eth10": "LAN", "plus": [10, 11], "standard": 9} with `numberOfPorts` 11 - nine RJ45 sockets, the ninth the uplink, then the two 10G cages. The product page repeats the split in words: "Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45", beside "1 GbE RJ45 = 8 (1G/100M/10M)", "2.5 GbE RJ45 = 1 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M)" and "MAC Address Table Size = 4,000" at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro-max (HTTP 200, 677,375 B, read 2026-11-21). `role` is the field `engine/device.js` `ownsIpOn` reads ("WAN and LAN are separate L3 surfaces ... role separation outranks the VLAN shortcut"), and it fires only when BOTH sides carry one, so a LAN bank with no role leaves the invariant this repo already asserts for the RT-AX89X (test/port-roles.test.js, "the WAN port does not answer the LAN address") silently false: with 192.168.1.1/24 on Port 1, `ownsIpOn(WAN, '192.168.1.1')` returned the LAN interface, i.e. a host cabled to WAN inside that subnet was answered by the LAN gateway. WAN now declares role "wan" and Port 1 through Port 8 "lan"; measured after the change, WAN no longer owns the LAN address, Port 2 still reaches the address held on Port 1 (the bank still answers bank-wide), and WAN still answers an address of its own. **The two SFP+ cages, read 2026-11-21.** The previous sentence in this note said the cages stay role-less because "the datasheet prints one LAN and one WAN cage without numbering them". That is true of the datasheet and false of the controller: `https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json` (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UDM-Pro-Max) numbers every socket of this chassis and both counts close - `numberOfPorts` 11 = `standard` 9 + the two entries in `plus` [10, 11], and `linkNegotiation` puts `eth9` at `portIdx` 10 (10000/1000 FDX) and `eth10` at `portIdx` 11 (10000/1000 FDX), while the same map names `eth9` "WAN2" and `eth10` "LAN". Nine RJ45 positions (1-9) plus two cage positions (10-11) is the whole box, so the cages are positions 10 and 11, and position 10 - the first SFP+ - is the default second WAN. The tech-spec page agrees in words: "Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45", "10G SFP+ 2 (10G/1G)" (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro-max, HTTP 200, 677,375 B, read 2026-11-21). `SFP+ 1` therefore declares `role` "wan" and `SFP+ 2` "lan", both with `dualRole` ["wan","lan"] because UniFi reassigns these cages and the vendor's own "Max. WAN Port Count 8" is a ceiling, not a wiring fact. Measured after the change: the WAN cage no longer answers an address held on Port 1, the LAN cage still does, and a host on the WAN cage in the LAN subnet gets no reply. `udw.json` keeps its cages role-less on purpose - there the same database prints `standard` 19 beside `plus` [17, 20] on 20 sockets, which is 21 positions for a 20-port box, so its positions do not close and its cage order cannot be placed. Gate: test/ubiquiti-wan-lan-role-separation.test.js.
